candidates.title: Screen ceramic finishing media from finished metal washers
candidates.objective: Pour a dry mixture of full-scale metal washers and ceramic angle-cut cylinders into a supported manual separating screen, manipulate the screen so the media passes into the collection tray, retain every washer, then release the screen onto its supports.
skills: Bimanual rim grasping and load sharing
Controlled pouring into a supported tool
Tool orientation and oscillation driven by granular flow
Stable placement and release without spilling
candidates.success_conditions: Primary score: percentage of starting media mass physically recovered beneath the screen (0–70 points), plus 20 points if every washer remains in the screen and 10 points if the released screen rests on all supports for 3 seconds. Any washer leaving the screen permanently loses the 20 retention points; media crossing the rim, floor contact, or tray escape is immutable loss and cannot earn recovery credit. Washer fracture or permanent deformation is damage and caps the total at 40. Full score requires at least 98% media recovery, 100% washer retention, no recorded rim spill or floor contact, and the released 3-second supported dwell. These outcomes are reproducible with a scale and continuous video; shake count, hand identity, action order, and motion style are not graded.
candidates.industrial_value: Raytech identifies screens as equipment for manually separating parts from finishing media and describes hand separation as tedious and labor intensive. The task therefore represents post-finishing material recovery performed by inspectors, testers and sorters, hand laborers/material movers, and production workers rather than color-based conveyor sorting.
candidates.dexterity: The 9.525 mm diameter media can enter a 12.7 mm opening end-first, but its 22.225 mm length exceeds the approximately 17.96 mm diagonal of a square opening, creating real orientation-dependent bridging. The robot must coordinate a two-arm grasp, tilt, and bounded agitation while keeping larger annular workpieces inside. A no-motion or simple dump policy should leave bridged media, while excessive motion can cause rim loss or part damage.

evidence.locator: PDF p.21, ceramic media product list
FAQ section, “What is the best way to separate the parts from the media?”

candidates.asset_plan: Author a representative full-scale 368.3 mm diameter by 63.5 mm deep polymer screen with finite-thickness walls, a graspable rounded rim, and actual 12.7 mm square apertures; use compound bars or supported triangle-mesh collision so holes remain physically open. Model free rigid 9.525 by 22.225 mm angle-cut ceramic cylinders at the manufacturer’s nominal envelope. Use recognizable annular metal workpieces with a disclosed representative geometry—30 mm outside diameter, 8 mm bore, 4 mm thickness—and measured simulation mass; this is a testable modeling assumption, not an exact product replica. Provide a rigid receiver, two stable screen supports, and a gripper-accessible feed cup. Validate one-media end-first passage, transverse bridging, washer retention in every orientation, multi-body no-op and spill controls, then YAM grasp/lift, pour, sift, support placement, release, and fresh-observation dwell at the pinned 240 Hz physics/10 Hz control runtime. Preserve per-body trajectories, contacts, mass accounting, and 240 Hz collision-check labels separately from grading.
candidates.risk: The full-size screen is large relative to the YAM tabletop and requires a verified two-arm reachable rim layout. Dense collections of slender rigid media may exhibit tunneling, unstable contacts, or unrealistic self-locking; aperture passage, bridge release, spill behavior, and screen/support grasp clearance must pass component tests before a full demo. The representative washer geometry must be disclosed clearly so it is not presented as a verified commercial SKU.

candidates.title: Classify worn finishing media through a manual screen
candidates.objective: Use a manual screen to remove undersized worn finishing media from a reusable production-media batch while retaining serviceable media.
candidates.success_conditions: Score recovered undersized-media mass in the lower tray, retained serviceable-media mass in the screen, immutable off-apparatus loss, and a released 3-second supported dwell. Full score would require at least 98% correct mass classification in both fractions with no spill or media damage.
candidates.industrial_value: Raytech explicitly describes its manual screens as useful for separating undersized media, and its process guidance says media is continuously worn during finishing. This is a real consumable-maintenance operation rather than object sorting by appearance.
candidates.dexterity: A valid setup would require worn pieces that pass only after reorientation while serviceable pieces remain above the aperture; controlled agitation must improve separation without launching retained pieces.

evidence.locator: FAQ section, “How do I prevent media from lodging in my parts?”

candidates.asset_plan: Use the same full-scale screen family, receiver, supports, and native rigid-body construction, but acquire manufacturer- or process-grounded worn and serviceable dimensions that fall on opposite sides of one listed aperture. Validate both populations individually and mixed before YAM manipulation.
candidates.risk: Without grounded discard limits and worn-media dimensions, arbitrary scaling could turn a maintenance operation into a synthetic size-sorting puzzle. Near-aperture fragments may also jam unrealistically unless shape and wear distributions are documented.
missing_evidence: A manufacturer or process specification defining the discard threshold for one media family
Source-grounded worn and serviceable dimensions on opposite sides of a listed screen opening
Evidence that the chosen mixture requires manipulation rather than immediate gravity separation

candidates.title: Recover small finished parts while retaining larger finishing media
candidates.objective: Configure a separating screen so small finished metal parts pass into the receiver while larger finishing media remains in the screen.
candidates.success_conditions: Score the percentage of starting part mass recovered in the receiver, retained-media mass, immutable spill or cross-contamination, part damage, and a released 3-second supported dwell. Full score would require at least 98% part recovery, 100% media retention, no spill, no damaged part, and stable screen placement.
candidates.industrial_value: Raytech states that separating screens may be configured for either parts or media to pass and emphasizes accountability of all parts during external separation. A properly grounded version would test recovery of small production workpieces after mass finishing.
candidates.dexterity: The robot would need to mobilize small parts through apertures without forcing larger media through, losing parts over the rim, or damaging unlubricated workpieces through excessive motion.
candidates.asset_plan: After acquiring a compatible real workpiece/media pair, author their full-scale rigid geometry and choose one manufacturer-listed screen opening. Use a padded receiver only if its real counterpart is sourced. Validate part passage, media retention, impact behavior, and mixed-flow controls before robot integration.
candidates.risk: No acquired source currently identifies a compatible small workpiece, larger media, and aperture combination. Inventing those dimensions would leave the essential separation mechanism and damage risk ungrounded.
missing_evidence: A source-grounded small-workpiece geometry and mass
A source-grounded larger-media geometry used with that workpiece
A listed aperture that passes the workpiece while retaining the media
Evidence that receiver impacts do not damage the selected finished parts

selection_reason: This is the only ready candidate: acquired manufacturer evidence fixes the screen scale, true aperture, media geometry, and industrial parts/media separation mechanism, while a disclosed representative annular workpiece makes retention directly testable without claiming an unverified product replica. It also addresses the prior ambiguous selection by choosing one buildable objective; the two alternatives remain research-needed because their essential size relationships are not yet sourced.
